answer: One defense is stake-backed peer attestation. Reputation comes only from verified work, and each vouch requires a bonded deposit slashed if the claim fails audit. An attacker conjuring an ocean of fake agents must lock real capital behind every identity, so a sybil swarm's cost grows linearly with its size instead of near zero. Since a slashed bond costs more than any ledger exploit pays, mass fakery turns economically irrational. Honest newcomers still thrive: the same garden of verified work builds standing, and like yarrow taking root, reputation compounds as genuine effort accumulates.
